messages.subject: Power analysis of Z-test
parts:
I have been using DISTANCE to calculate primate densities in a forest in
Uganda and I have used the Z-test (p381 in Buckland et al. 1993) to test
for differences between density estimates between two successive census
counts. I have been asked by one of the referees of one of my
manuscripts to calculate the power of this Z-test to detect a
difference.

I have looked at a couple of power analysis programs and both need a
sample size to calculate the power of a Z-test. What is the sample size
when I am using the density and standard errors calculated by DISTANCE
in the Z-test. Presumably it is a function of the number of primate
groups seen and the number of transects? Can anyone help me with this?

Andy Plumptre
